title: Investigate tenant upgrade deadlock caused by concurrent Helm hook executions; ship surgical hotpatch and automated recovery job
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported tenant upgrades stuck in 'Upgrading' for >30 minutes after a scheduled on-prem Helm-based control plane upgrade. Affected tenants experienced blocked inference requests and failing healthchecks. This ticket drives diagnosis, a low-risk surgical hotpatch to break the deadlock, an automated recovery job to reconcile stuck tenants, and long-term mitigations to prevent recurrence.

Observed behavior: Operator reconcile loops show two controller workers attempting to process the same tenant upgrade concurrently. Helm post-upgrade hooks that annotate tenant CRs are sometimes retried; meanwhile an idempotency bug in the KV schema migration obtains a tenant-scoped transaction lock and never releases it when preflight webhook responses are delayed. The result: tenant enters a state where finalizer removal is blocked, helm_release hook waits indefinitely, and normal reconcile cannot progress.

Why this matters: Blocked tenants lose inference throughput and require manual intervention; customers opened escalations with SRE and PMs. This is regressional relative to previous upgrade behavior and correlates with load spikes during staged upgrades.
repro_steps:
1) Deploy onprem operator image with new helm chart to a test cluster with 50 tenant namespaces. 2) Trigger staged upgrade using our upgrade orchestrator with concurrency=4 and helm hooks enabled. 3) Introduce a synthetic 5s delay in the mutating webhook (fold into CI via webhook-proxy). 4) Observe reconcile logs: two workers attempt to modify tenant CR simultaneously; KV migration acquires lock but does not clean up if webhook response delayed >3s. 5) Tenant CR remains in 'Upgrading' and helm_release hook is pending.

Note: Reproduction reliably occurs when webhook latency >=3000ms and concurrent upgrade workers >=3.
current_workaround: 1) On impacted clusters, scale operator replicas to 1 to serialize reconciles (temporary). 2) Run manual repair: kubectl annotate tenant <X> operator.redwood.io/force-unlock=true to trigger repair controller (internal script). 3) If annotation fails, run repair job provided below to forcibly remove helm hook finalizer and replay kv migration in a short-lived job. 4) Engage SRE to coordinate rolling restart of the operator only after snapshotting KV to avoid partial writes.
proposed_fix:
Short term (hotpatch): ship operator patch v0.0.7-hotfix that changes tenant reconcile to use a lease-backed fast-fail for KV migration locks and adds a safety timeout to helm hook wait of 45s. Include a one-off k8s Job 'tenant-upgrade-repair' that atomically: verifies tenant state, clears stuck finalizers if KV lock is expired, replays idempotent migration steps, and emits audit events.

Long term: 1) Rework KV migration to be fully idempotent and to always release locks via deferred cleanup path. 2) Add preflight upgrade check that simulates webhook responses and rejects upgrade if >500ms median. 3) Add integration test that runs staged upgrades with injected webhook latencies. 4) Add alerting for sustained helm hook waits >30s per-tenant and a dashboard for upgrade throughput and per-tenant lock acquisition time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hotfix operator image built and smoke-tested in canary cluster, with no regressions on normal reconciles.
- tenant-upgrade-repair k8s Job reviewed, added to operator toolbox, and verified on two customer-like clusters by SRE.
- Runbook updated with exact remediation commands and escalation contacts.
- Post-deploy monitoring: no new stuck-upgrade incidents in next 72h on canary; rollout to customers scheduled.
- Follow-up tasks (idempotency, preflight checks, tests) are filed as separate PM/ENG tickets.
postmortem_actions: Add helm-hook-wait SLI and burn-rate alert
Implement KV lock TTL with reconciler cleanup
Create synthetic-latency upgrade test in CI
Document operator scaling tradeoffs during upgrades
notes: Engineering lead (Mateo) paired with SRE (Lin) and Customer Success for two escalations (CustA, CustB). Legal/compliance notified for tenants with strict SLAs. Avoid changing customer data paths in hotpatch; the repair job only touches control-plane metadata and uses conservative timeouts.
